title: PISA 2025: la secundaria es donde se juega el futuro de esta generación
gist: PISA 2025 shows Latin American 15-year-olds fell another 11 points in reading and 4 in mathematics between 2022 and 2025, leaving the region's 13 participating countries 93 points behind the OECD in math (roughly four to five years of schooling) with 76% below the minimum math threshold; the authors argue secondary education, not primary, is where the region's productivity future is decided.

themes.theme: Magnitud de la caída en PISA 2025

insights.claim: Latin American PISA scores fell 11 points in reading and 4 points in mathematics between 2022 and 2025 and were flat in science, extending a decline that began in 2018.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: A third consecutive negative PISA cycle marks a structural, not pandemic-specific, human-capital deterioration in the region.
insights.locator: Los aprendizajes de los estudiantes de secundaria

insights.claim: The thirteen Latin American countries in PISA 2025 sit 93 points below the OECD average in mathematics, 83 in science and 72 in reading; at the OECD's own conversion of about 20 points per year of schooling, that is four to five years of learning behind.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: A four-to-five-year learning gap caps the skill ceiling of the region's future labor force and its tradable-sector competitiveness.
insights.quote: nuestros jóvenes están entre cuatro y cinco años de aprendizaje por detrás de los de la OCDE
insights.locator: Lo que muestran los datos de América Latina

insights.claim: A majority of Latin American 15-year-olds fall below PISA's basic-functioning floor: 59% in reading, 57% in science and 76% in mathematics, versus 31%, 26% and 35% in the OECD.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Three of four regional teenagers cannot mathematically represent a simple situation, which is the binding constraint on any automation or upskilling agenda.
insights.locator: Y en la región, la mayoría de los estudiantes

insights.claim: One in two students in the region is below the minimum in all three subjects simultaneously, against one in five in the OECD.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Compounded deficits across subjects mean remediation costs are far higher than single-subject gap statistics suggest.
insights.locator: Uno de cada dos estudiantes de la región

insights.claim: The share of students below the minimum is still growing: five Latin American countries saw a significant increase in students below the reading floor between 2022 and 2025, and three in mathematics.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: The tail is thickening, not stabilizing, so the base-case is further deterioration absent policy change.
insights.locator: Y ese grupo de estudiantes, debajo de ese piso

insights.claim: No country in the region improved significantly in reading or mathematics; mathematics fell by more than 8 points in Argentina, Guatemala, Chile and Peru, and reading fell by more than 8 points in Guatemala, Paraguay, Peru, Argentina, Chile and Colombia.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Country-level differentiation matters: Peru, Argentina and Chile are deteriorating fastest on both axes.
insights.locator: Ningún país de la región mejoró significativamente

insights.claim: Only three of the sixteen education systems worldwide that improved in science are Latin American — Costa Rica, El Salvador and Uruguay — with Costa Rica posting its first significant improvement since it began participating in PISA.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: These three are the region's only positive-momentum education systems and the natural case studies for what works.
insights.locator: La buena noticia está en ciencias

insights.claim: Eight education systems improved significantly in all three PISA subjects — Cambodia, the United Arab Emirates, the Philippines, Georgia, Jordan, Montenegro, Thailand and Turkey — and several started from levels similar to Guatemala or the Dominican Republic, proving low starting points are not destiny.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Rapid system-level learning gains are achievable from a low base, which undercuts the fatalism that income levels determine learning outcomes.
insights.locator: En el resto del mundo, ocho sistemas educativos

insights.claim: The OECD attributes the global reading decline to four interrelated factors: lost student attention, worse classroom conditions (more interruptions, less teaching time, more bullying), wide within-class ability spread that teachers cannot handle, and less reading for pleasure as social media and video games take time.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Attention capture by consumer platforms is now showing up as a measurable macro human-capital cost, a theme regulators may eventually price.
insights.locator: La OCDE atribuye la caída global en lectura

insights.claim: The share of 'hurried readers' — fast and wrong — has nearly doubled since 2018 in PISA data.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: A concrete, measurable marker of the attention-erosion thesis that can be tracked across future PISA cycles.
insights.quote: los "lectores apresurados" —rápidos y equivocados— casi se duplicaron desde 2018
insights.locator: Los estudiantes perdieron atención

insights.claim: Classroom climate is what most distinguishes Latin America: twelve of the region's thirteen countries exceed the OECD average on noise and disorder in class, with Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay leading the world measurement.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Classroom-order interventions are a cheap, underused lever in the region relative to technology or curriculum spending.
insights.locator: Pero nos distingue el clima del aula

insights.claim: The pandemic is not a clean explanation for the learning decline: countries with school closures of similar duration had very different results, though it may be an underlying factor, since PISA 2025 test-takers were 10 or 11 when schools closed — the age of transition from learning to read to reading to learn.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Blaming Covid closures alone is analytically lazy; the decline predates and outlasts them, implying a slower, structural drag.
insights.locator: ¿fue la pandemia? ¿Es la inteligencia artificial?

themes.theme: IA y aprendizaje: la dosis importa

insights.claim: PISA 2025 measured student use of artificial intelligence for the first time, and in OECD countries students who never use AI to summarize texts score better than those who do.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: The first large cross-country dataset on AI use and measured learning outcomes — a reference point for the edtech investment case.
insights.locator: PISA 2025 mide el uso de la inteligencia artificial por primera vez

insights.claim: In Latin America moderate use of AI is associated with better PISA results while daily use is associated with worse ones, suggesting AI helps when it adds to student effort and hinders when it replaces it.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: A dose-response frame for AI in education: products that substitute for effort may destroy the learning they claim to deliver, a product-design and regulatory risk for edtech.
insights.quote: la IA parece ayudar cuando suma al esfuerzo del estudiante y estorbar cuando lo reemplaza
insights.locator: En países de la OCDE, los estudiantes que nunca la usan

insights.claim: Only thirteen Latin American countries took part in PISA 2025 out of 91 participating countries and economies worldwide; Bolivia has never participated, Honduras only once, most Caribbean countries do not participate, and Jamaica and Panama dropped out after 2022.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Data coverage is itself a governance signal: countries that stop measuring remove the feedback loop that makes reform possible.
insights.quote: Ese es el peor escenario: no saber.
insights.locator: Una digresión sobre la participación

insights.claim: Measuring learning is framed as taking a patient's temperature: the risk of bad news is the price of knowing how much improvement is needed, and refusing to measure is the worst outcome.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: A transferable governance heuristic — treat willingness to be measured as a leading indicator of reform credibility.
insights.locator: Cuando uno mide, siempre corre el riesgo

themes.theme: Qué hacer: la secundaria como palanca

insights.claim: Two of every three working adults in Latin America today have no more than a secondary education, so whatever they learned in those years is the skill base the region's labor market runs on.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Links weak secondary schooling directly to the region's productivity ceiling — the transmission channel from PISA scores to GDP growth.
insights.quote: dos de cada tres adultos que hoy trabajan en América Latina no tienen más que secundaria
insights.locator: Qué hacer: la secundaria tiene que garantizar los aprendizajes

insights.claim: Students arrive in secondary school already far behind: at the end of sixth grade 62% do not reach the minimum level in reading and 74% do not reach it in mathematics, so teaching must start from where students actually are rather than from where the curriculum says they should be.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Teaching-at-the-right-level plus structured remediation is the highest-return intervention identified, and a market for adaptive assessment tools.
insights.locator: Empezar por donde están los estudiantes

insights.claim: Adaptive platforms and AI tutors can extend individualized support efficiently, but only with effective teacher accompaniment alongside them.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Defines the buy-side requirement for edtech procurement in the region: tools bundled with teacher support, not standalone licenses.
insights.locator: Las plataformas adaptativas y los tutores de IA

insights.claim: Dropout is predictable rather than sudden — absences, falling grades and behavior problems are early disengagement signals already captured in many countries' data — and preventing dropout is far more cost-effective than bringing a young person back after they leave.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Early-warning systems built on existing administrative data are a low-cost, high-return deployment of analytics in public education.
insights.locator: Llegar antes que la deserción

insights.claim: Curricula in the region are overloaded, and the fix is to define what students must master per grade and allow time to teach it well; a longer school day helps only if used well, which in some countries means moving from two or three shifts to full-day schooling and in others simply getting students to class every day.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Time-on-task and curricular focus are near-zero-capex reforms relative to infrastructure or device spending.
insights.locator: Enseñar mejor lo esencial

insights.claim: Technical secondary education that pays off in the labor market is neither easy nor cheap: it requires workshops and equipment, teachers who know the trade, real links to firms, employer-recognized certifications and career guidance.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Sets a realistic cost base for TVET programs, a recurring underestimation in regional education budgets and donor projects.
insights.locator: Muchos jóvenes saldrán directo a trabajar

insights.claim: Demanding better results must be paired with merit-based teacher careers, continuous coaching and materials, plus trained principals with authority and less administrative load.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Accountability without support fails; the pairing is the design rule for judging any teacher-reform announcement.
insights.locator: Fortalecer la profesión docente

insights.claim: These actions only move learning if they arrive integrated and simultaneously in every school, which requires sustained political commitment, continuous measurement, correction of what does not work and visible results so families can demand improvement.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Screens reform announcements: piecemeal, single-component programs should be discounted as unlikely to move outcomes.
insights.quote: Para que tengan impacto en los aprendizajes, estas acciones tienen que llegar integradas, al mismo tiempo.
insights.locator: Para que tengan impacto en los aprendizajes
